# Records you need to keep
## Record keeping exceptions
### Total work-related expenses $300 or less
If your total claim for work-related expenses is more than $300, you must have full written evidence to support all your claims.

web.title: myTax 2026 Other work-related expenses - Australian Taxation Office
web.description:
# myTax 2026 Other work-related expenses
## Things to know
If your total claim for work-related expenses is more than $300, you must have written evidence to prove your claims.

## Completing this section
If you exceed the $300 limit, you must have [written evidence](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/income-deductions-offsets-and-records/records-you-need-to-keep) of all your expenses (such as receipts or invoices), unless an [exception](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/income-deductions-offsets-and-records/records-you-need-to-keep#ato-Recordkeepingexceptions) applies.

web.title: Work-related expenses | Australian Taxation Office
web.description:
# Work-related expenses
## Rules for written evidence to substantiate deductions
Your client must have written evidence to prove their claims if the total claims exceed $300. The records must prove the total amount, not just the amount over $300.

web.title: myTax 2026 Claiming deductions - Australian Taxation Office
web.description:
# myTax 2026 Claiming deductions
## Record keeping for work-related expenses
### Total work-related expenses more than $300
If the total amount of deductions you're claiming is more than $300, you must have written evidence (such as a receipt or invoice) to [show you incurred and weren't reimbursed for the expenses you claim](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/income-deductions-offsets-and-records/records-you-need-to-keep).

The written evidence and records you keep must prove the total amount you claim, not just the amount over $300.
